example.name: designing_concurrent_processor
example.description: Designing a concurrent data processor using Go's concurrency primitives.
example.context: Need to process a large number of items concurrently with controlled parallelism and proper error handling.
example.workflow:
Understand requirements
Process 10,000+ items Limit to 10 concurrent workers Support cancellation Collect all results and errors
Design worker pool pattern
Job channel - buffered channel for input Result channel - buffered channel for output Worker goroutines - fixed number of workers sync.WaitGroup - wait for completion context.Context - cancellation support
<step number="3> Define types
type Job struct { ID string Data []byte }
type Result struct { JobID string Data []byte Err error }
type Processor struct { numWorkers int jobChan chan Job resultChan chan Result }
Design worker function
func (p *Processor) worker(ctx context.Context, wg *sync.WaitGroup) { defer wg.Done() for { select { case <-ctx.Done(): return case job, ok := <-p.jobChan: if !ok { return } result := p.processJob(ctx, job) p.resultChan <- result } } }
Plan error handling
Collect all errors in results
Continue processing on individual failures
Use context for cancellation on fatal errors
Provide summary of successes and failures
Design testing strategy
Unit test for worker function Integration test for full processor Benchmark for performance Test cancellation behavior
